title: Audit Export: RBAC-gate destination management + audit log config-change events
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: RBAC now gates Audit Export destination management APIs. Audit events are emitted for create/update/delete/pause/resume and filter changes (no secrets logged).
body:
Summary: This PR adds (1) RBAC permission gates to the audit export destination management endpoints and (2) audit log entries for export destination configuration changes. Motivation: SIEM-ready audit export is a security-sensitive control. We need explicit permissions to create/modify export destinations and we need an audit trail for who changed what (SOC2/ISO evidence, incident investigations). This is also a prerequisite for Console UX so we can hide/disable actions based on role. Scope / behavior: RBAC: Introduces a new permission set under the workspace scope: audit_export.destinations.read, audit_export.destinations.write, audit_export.destinations.pause_resume, audit_export.destinations.test. The audit-export control plane handlers now require these permissions for: GET /v1/audit-export/destinations* (read), POST/PUT/DELETE (write), POST /:id/pause and /:id/resume (pause_resume), POST /:id/test (test). Default is deny: if the permission is not present, the request returns 403 with error_id and required_permission in the response metadata. Role mapping: Workspace Owner/Admin gets all audit_export.* by default; a new built-in role preset "Security Admin" is granted read + pause_resume + test but not write/delete (intended for security operators). (Note: role preset wiring is behind the existing enterprise_rbac_presets flag; for beta tenants we will grant explicitly.) Audit logging: Emits audit events (schema v1) on the following transitions: audit.export.destination.created, audit.export.destination.updated, audit.export.destination.deleted, audit.export.destination.paused, audit.export.destination.resumed, audit.export.destination.filters_updated, audit.export.destination.credentials_rotated. Events include destination_id, destination_type (splunk|datadog|s3), workspace_id, environment, actor (user/service), request_id, and a redacted change summary. No secrets are ever logged (tokens, api keys, raw headers). For update operations we record a field-level allowlisted diff (e.g., endpoint_host, index, bucket, region, filter_rule_ids, enabled_state) and omit credential fields entirely. Implementation details: Adds authz checks in the audit-export API layer (before hitting storage) and in the shared Console backend router used by the UI. Adds an AuditExportAuditEmitter helper that constructs schema-v1 compliant events and sends via the existing audit log producer (async, best-effort; failures are logged and counted but do not fail the original request). Adds unit tests for: permission matrix for each endpoint; ensure 403 for missing permission; ensure audit events are produced for create/update/delete/pause/resume; ensure redaction (no token/api_key leakage) with snapshot assertions. Rollout notes: No behavior change for tenants without the SIEM export beta flag (endpoints remain inaccessible). For beta tenants, requests that previously succeeded with generic admin rights will now require explicit permissions. Solutions Eng will need to ensure beta roles are set correctly in onboarding. Out of scope: Audit events for delivery-plane failures/backlog; replay tooling permissions; additional fine-grained permissions per destination type; retroactive backfill of audit trail. Testing: Unit tests added for authz + audit emitter. Manual: verified in staging with a beta tenant: (a) Workspace Admin can create and edit destination; (b) Security Admin can pause/resume and send test but cannot edit endpoint; (c) audit log stream shows config-change events with redacted payload. Screenshots/log excerpts are in the linked Linear ticket ENG-13933. Changed areas (high-level): services/control-plane/audit_export/* (handlers + authz), packages/rbac/policies/* (new permissions + role preset), packages/audit/events/* (new event types + emitter), console-backend/routes/audit_export.ts (gates), tests/* (unit + snapshots). Commits: 1) rbac: add audit_export permissions + policy bundle 2) audit-export: gate destination handlers w/ required permissions 3) audit: emit config-change events (schema v1) 4) tests: authz matrix + redaction snapshots 5) docs: internal comment updates for required permissions

Review conversation (highlights): Marcus Lin (Security Eng): "Can we ensure we never include destination headers/query params in the audit event? Some customers embed tokens in endpoint URLs." Benji Okafor: "Good catch. Updated change-summary builder to store only endpoint_host (parsed host) and to drop full URL entirely. Added a redaction test that fails if 'token=' appears anywhere in payload." Kevin Osei: "We should also audit filter updates separately from general updates so SIEM correlation rules can watch for noise-reduction attempts." Benji Okafor: "Split into audit.export.destination.filters_updated and audit.export.destination.updated; filters_updated triggers only when filter rules change (including include/exclude lists)." Ethan Park: "Do we want audit logging to be blocking?" Benji Okafor: "Kept it async/best-effort like other control plane audit emitters; we record a metric audit_export.audit_emit_failures_total and log with error_id for investigation." Chloe Martin: "Console needs to know which permission is missing to show a helpful error." Benji Okafor: "403 payload includes required_permission and error_id; Console can map to the docs/help text. Also added a small helper in console-backend to pass through." Felix Schneider: "Any chance the diff payload gets big for large filters?" Benji Okafor: "We only emit field allowlist + counts for large lists; detailed filter rule bodies are not included. Added a max_payload_bytes guard with truncation marker." Approvals: Marcus Lin approved after redaction changes; Kevin Osei approved; Ethan Park approved; Chloe Martin approved for Console integration.

CI: redwood/unit-tests (pass), redwood/lint (pass), redwood/integration-tests (pass), security-sast (pass). Merge: Squash merged into main.
